sections.h2: Which Warren County offices deal with property tax?
sections.html:
Two elected offices split the work. The Warren County Auditor values property and administers credits, and the Warren County Treasurer sends the bills and takes payment. The auditor's office is at 406 Justice Drive in Lebanon, and its real estate department answers at 513-695-1235.

The auditor's real estate page says the office maintains records on about 91,400 parcels, covering ownership, legal description, property address, building description, appraised value and the transfer history that feeds the tax list. The treasurer posts rate sheets for every year from 2004 through 2025, so a seller can look up how a parcel's levies have moved.

Value complaints go to a third body, the Board of Revision, made up of the auditor, the treasurer and the president of the county commissioners.

sections.h2: How does Warren County value a house for tax?
sections.html:
Each parcel is appraised at estimated fair market value and taxed at 35 percent of it, which is how the auditor's appraisal page describes Ohio's common level of assessment. Every parcel gets a site visit in a general reappraisal at least once every six years, and a triennial update adjusts values in the third year between those cycles, usually by percentage changes drawn from local sales.

New construction and changes in use are valued every year. The tax lien date is January 1, so ownership and use on that day fix the bill payable the following year.

The auditor's own FAQ says most increases follow the state-required reappraisal, and that without new construction or new levies, bills tend to stay close to the same level between updates. A school levy passed by voters in a district raises bills for the parcels inside it, which is why two similar homes in different school districts can pay different amounts. Warren County has ten school districts, from Carlisle and Clinton-Massie to Kings, Lebanon, Mason and Springboro, plus a career center.

sections.h2: When are Warren County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Ohio real estate tax is billed in two halves. For tax year 2025 the treasurer's page printed February 25, 2026 for the first half and August 12, 2026 for the second. The August date was an extension the Tax Commissioner approved after House Bill 186's inflation cap credit delayed the second-half bills, and the treasurer asked owners to wait for the bill rather than send an estimate.

Payment options include the myWarrenCountyOhio portal, the phone line at 513-496-2931, and the treasurer's counter, open 7:30 am to 4:30 pm Monday through Friday. The page also posts a penalty remission application, a military extension application and a Notice of Possible Tax Adjustment.

Late charges come from Revised Code 323.121: an unpaid half draws a ten percent penalty, cut in half when the whole amount arrives within ten days of the deadline. Interest accrues on delinquent taxes at the rate set under section 5703.47.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Warren County property value?
sections.html:
Owners who think the auditor's number is too high file a complaint on form DTE 1 between January 1 and March 31 of the following tax year. A notary must witness the signature of the owner or the owner's attorney.

What the board decides is market value for land and buildings together, never the tax dollars or rates. Because the owner carries the burden of proof, a weak case can leave the value alone or push it up. The board sends notice at least ten days before the recorded hearing and later mails or emails a decision letter to each party.

  • The auditor's FAQ names three good kinds of evidence: a recent sale for less than the county's value, a recent fee appraisal, and proof of damage or defects that hurt the home's worth.
  • The board may also request purchase or lease agreements, closing statements, construction cost records, rent rolls and income and expense statements.
  • Get supporting papers to the board before the hearing date.

sections.h2: What tax breaks does Warren County offer homeowners?
sections.html:
The auditor runs several programs, and each ties to your principal residence on January 1. A person can claim a homestead or owner-occupied reduction on only one Ohio home.

Warren County auditor filing rules for homeowner credits and appeals
ProgramWho qualifiesForm and filing time
Homestead ExemptionAge 65 or older, permanently and totally disabled, or a surviving spouse aged 59 or older of a past participantDTE 105A, received by December 31
Owner-Occupied CreditHomeowner living in the property on January 1DTE 105C, filed on or before December 31
Board of Revision complaintAny owner disputing the market valueDTE 1, filed January 1 to March 31

The homestead page capped income for the 2026 tax year at $41,000 of 2025 Ohio adjusted gross income. Owners who miss the cutoff can reapply the next year, when the state may raise it. A disability claim needs Certificate of Disability form DTE 105E or another accepted certification.

Two other reductions are worth knowing. Damaged or destroyed buildings can earn a value deduction on form DTE 26, filed by December 31 for damage in the first nine months of a year or by January 31 for damage in the last three, with the share granted set by the quarter: 100 percent for January to March, 75 for April to June, 50 for July to September and 25 for October to December. Farmland in the CAUV program is valued on expected farm income, open to farms over 10 acres in commercial use for three years and to smaller ones grossing at least $2,500 a year, with a $25 first-time filing fee and a payback of up to three years of savings if the use changes.

sections.h2: What changes on the tax side when a Warren County home sells?
sections.html:
The auditor transfers the deed on the tax list before the recorder sees it. Its fees run $1.00 per thousand dollars of price as the mandatory conveyance fee and $2.00 per thousand as the county transfer tax, plus $0.50 per parcel.

The state's statement of value, set out in section 319.202, asks whether the home's taxes are reduced under the homestead or owner-occupied credit statute, and whether the land carried CAUV value. A yes means a sworn paper estimating the reduction or the recoupment, signed by buyer and seller. The statement also reminds the buyer to tell the auditor if the home later stops qualifying for the reduction.

Warren County's rental rules show up here too: when the property is residential rental property, the auditor stamps the deed with a note that the new owner must file the registration information.

sections.h2: What should a Warren County seller with back taxes do?
sections.html:
Call the treasurer before listing and ask for a written payoff that includes penalties and interest, so the title company can use it at closing. The Application for Remission of Late Payment Penalties on the treasurer's page is the way to ask for relief.

The county also runs forfeited land sales, and the auditor's home page announced one for November 9, 2026. Ask either office how a delinquent parcel moves toward that kind of sale, and settle the balance early.

faqs.q: Who sends the property tax bill in Warren County, Ohio?
faqs.a: The Warren County Treasurer does. The auditor sets the value, and the treasurer bills, collects and posts rate sheets. Payment options include myWarrenCountyOhio, and phone at 513-496-2931.

faqs.q: What percent of market value does Warren County tax?
faqs.a: Thirty-five percent of appraised value is the taxable value, as the auditor's appraisal page explains. The auditor reappraises every parcel at least once in six years and updates values in the third year between.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to challenge a Warren County valuation?
faqs.a: March 31 closes the window. A DTE 1 complaint can go to the auditor starting January 1 of the following tax year, and the signature has to be notarized.

faqs.q: What income limit applies to the Warren County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: For the 2026 tax year the auditor's page lists $41,000 of 2025 Ohio adjusted gross income. Eligible applicants are 65 or older, permanently and totally disabled, or surviving spouses aged 59 or older, and the application is due at the auditor's office by December 31.

faqs.q: Can I get Warren County late-payment penalties removed?
faqs.a: You can apply. The treasurer's page posts an Application for Remission of Late Payment Penalties and a Military Extension Application. Under Ohio law, paying the full amount within ten days of the due date also cuts the penalty in half.
